LESSON: PAINTING AND MOSAIC

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.4: Painting and Mosaic

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Painting and Mosaic. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we use pictures in our daily lives?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify primary and secondary colours on the colour wheel
2. create a mosaic picture to apply the characteristics
3. appreciate painting and mosaic as picture making techniques

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PAINTING AND MOSAIC
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Painting and Mosaic helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: PAINTING AND MOSAIC
Study Painting and Mosaic like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify primary and secondary colours on the colour wheel

What this means
In this part you learn to identify primary and secondary colours on the colour wheel. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify primary and secondary colours on the colour wheel.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Painting and Mosaic” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify primary and secondary colours on the colour wheel. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create a mosaic picture to apply the characteristics

What this means
In this part you learn to create a mosaic picture to apply the characteristics. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a mosaic picture to apply the characteristics.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Painting and Mosaic in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a mosaic picture to apply the characteristics. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate painting and mosaic as picture making techniques

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate painting and mosaic as picture making techniques. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate painting and mosaic as picture making techniques.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate painting and mosaic as picture making techniques. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Painting and Mosaic is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Painting and Mosaic” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify primary and secondary colours on the colour wheel)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Painting and Mosaic in your own words. (skill: create a mosaic picture to apply the characteristics)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate painting and mosaic as picture making techniques)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Painting and Mosaic to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify primary and secondary colours on the colour wheel.
3. Practise this skill: create a mosaic picture to apply the characteristics.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate painting and mosaic as picture making techniques.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Painting and Mosaic from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Painting and Mosaic: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Painting and Mosaic?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we use pictures in our daily lives?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Painting and Mosaic means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify primary and secondary colours on the colour wheel.
5. Be able to: create a mosaic picture to apply the characteristics.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
